channel.title: Kronos Fusion Energy
channel.description: Open papers, preprints, deposits, and whitepapers from Kronos Fusion Energy — the fusion company that shows its work. Conceptual design and simulation study; no machine has been built.

item.title: Paper 1 — The spherical-tokamak tritium / helium-3 breeder (HYPERION)
item.description: Physics, design, and conditional economics of HYPERION, a compact deuterium-tritium spherical tokamak that breeds tritium, helium-3, and 14 MeV neutrons. Open data and code deposited under CC BY 4.0 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21746157). Submitted to IOP; arXiv preprint on posting.

item.title: Paper 2 — The D–³He tandem-mirror generator (Aegis / MetroVolt)
item.description: The physics of the Kronos generator: a deuterium-helium-3 tandem mirror with direct energy conversion. Physics only. Open data and code deposited under CC BY 4.0 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21746479). Submitted to IOP; arXiv preprint on posting.

item.title: Whitepaper library — 100 short papers
item.description: One hundred one-idea whitepapers covering the breeder, the generator, the fuel logic, and the named open gaps. Every figure traces to the openly deposited simulation program.

item.title: Why Kronos builds the breeder first
item.description: Every fusion economy needs a fuel supply before it needs a power plant. HYPERION is the fuel supply.

item.title: The gain is solved, not scaled
item.description: HYPERION's design gain Q = 3.424 comes from power balance, not from an extrapolated scaling law.

item.title: Helium-3 as a co-product
item.description: The breeder's helium-3 stream is the fuel the burner will eventually run on.

item.title: Two housings, one machine
item.description: Aegis and MetroVolt are the same deuterium-helium-3 tandem-mirror generator in two housings.

item.title: Why a mirror
item.description: The directed-particle ceiling is what moved the burner from a tokamak to an open mirror.

item.title: Fixed-site, not shipboard
item.description: Aegis is a fixed defense-installation generator; the naval case is closed negative.

item.title: Low-neutron, never aneutronic
item.description: D-helium-3 is low-neutron (~6.5%), not aneutronic; the honest term is low-neutron.

item.title: Named gates, not hidden assumptions
item.description: The thermal barrier, electron direct conversion, and synchrotron closure are stated as measurable gates.

item.title: Design evolution — labeled history
item.description: How the Kronos design moved from a spherical tokamak, through fuel eliminations, to a two-machine breeder-plus-mirror program. Superseded values kept with era labels.
